mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies Registry or competent UBO registry in the shareholder's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board resolution of the corporate shareholder authorizing the incorporation of the Spanish SL, the share capital subscription and the appointment of officers
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or officially registered minutes in the shareholder's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney naming the Spanish incorporation agent or attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in country of origin; accepted by Spanish notary upon apostille and translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Signed AML/CFT questionnaire, PEP declaration and source-of-wealth statement for each natural-person UBO and manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: UBO or manager, notarized before a Spanish notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if executed abroad, otherwise Spanish notarial authentication

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, UBOs, and relevant counterparties against the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, Spanish SEPBLAC alerts, and the Bank of Spain reporting registers. Politically exposed persons are subject to enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds verification, and senior-level approval before incorporation. Any red flags in the dairy commodity trade, including unusual third-country transit, round-tripping, or cash settlement, are referred to SEPBLAC under Article 18 of Ley 10/2010.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Central Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Central) - Denominaciones Sociales section, accessible through the official Registradores de España online portal (www.registradores.org)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be written in the 27-letter Spanish alphabet; non-Spanish scripts must be transliterated into Latin characters in accordance with the registry spelling rules. The name must be a permissible SL denomination, must include a valid ending such as S.L. or S.L.U., and must not be identical, misleading, or conflicting with existing registered names or protected trademarks.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name certificate is rejected, the applicant may file a reconsideration petition (recurso de reposición) with the Registro Mercantil Central within one month. If the reconsideration is denied, an administrative appeal (recurso de alzada) may be filed with the General Directorate of Registries and Notaries of the Ministry of Justice within three months, followed by judicial review before the administrative courts. An alternative name can be requested at any time.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible as the sole registered office for a Spanish SL. A physical address within the relevant province is required for legal notifications, registry filings, and tax authority correspondence. Virtual-only arrangements may be tolerated by the registry if a physical mailbox is maintained but will not satisfy commercial substance requirements for bank account opening, export licenses, or AML risk rating.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Estimated 15% likelihood of an unannounced physical inspection of the registered office within the first 24 months for a low-risk dairy commodity trader; the risk rises to approximately 35% if SEPBLAC identifies a non-resident ownership chain with no local employees or physical assets.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark per document, approximately EUR 180-250

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for a Madrid or Valencia physical address service

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial fee for attestation, approximately EUR 60-100

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 1/2010, de 5 de marzo, de Sociedades de Responsabilidad Limitada (LSRL), Articles 1-10
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución de Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum subscribed capital of 3,000 EUR fully subscribed at incorporation with at least 25% paid up in cash; proof of bank deposit required, no separate escrow account mandated
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The First Board of Directors of the proposed Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada resolves as follows: 1. To fully subscribe to the share capital in the proportions and amounts detailed in the Articles of Association. 2. To establish the registered office at [Address], Spain, as the corporate domicile. 3. To appoint [Name] as Managing Director and [Name] as Director, granting full representation powers. 4. To approve the Articles of Association and authorize their execution and registration. 5. To empower the Managing Director to carry out all acts of incorporation and commence business activities. Adopted unanimously on [Date].

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a notary to prepare and execute the public deed of incorporation. Submit shareholder details, draft articles, and capital subscription proof. The notary will verify compliance with legal requirements.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Submit additional documentation or request amendment to articles if the notary queries the application

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the notarized deed via the electronic headquarters of the Registro Mercantil. Pay the registration fee and obtain the certificate of registration. The company will receive the tomo, folio, and inscription number.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If application is queried, provide missing documents within the stipulated period or appeal procedurally

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply online for the NIF using the registration certificate from the Registro Mercantil. Submit all incorporation documents to obtain the fiscal identification.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If rejected, correct the application and resubmit within 5 days

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No discharge of wastewater, VOCs, or hazardous waste; comply with general environmental protection regulations for commercial premises

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain fire safety certification from the local fire brigade, perform structural safety inspections if applicable, and secure occupational health and safety clearance from the labor authority

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), the Spanish State Tax Administration Agency; primary digital portal: sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es; the Censo de Empresarios, Profesionales y Retenedores is managed through modelo 036/037 forms on this portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For the Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL): upon deed of incorporation before a notary, AEAT assigns a provisional NIF/CIF; the definitive NIF is issued after inscription in the Registro Mercantil and the filing of modelo 036 for the definitive census registration. Foreign entities acting without a permanent establishment in Spain must appoint a Spanish-resident tax representative (representante fiscal) and file modelo 036 to obtain a non-resident NIF; importers/exporters must additionally obtain an EORI number from the Departamento de Aduanas e Impuestos Especiales (Customs and Excise Department) before lodging export declarations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spain does not operate a US-style check-the-box regime, but offers specific statutory elections: (i) option to be taxed as a consolidated corporate tax group (régimen de consolidación fiscal) with binding application for at least three years; (ii) election for the ETVE (Empresa de Tenencia de Valores Extranjeros) regime granting an intra-group exemption for foreign dividends and capital gains on non-Spanish qualifying holdings; (iii) VAT election between the general deduction system and the pro-rata rules (prorrata general vs prorrata especial); (iv) election for the simplified VAT regime (régimen simplificado) by small traders below statutory turnover limits; and (v) ATAD-aligned hybrid mismatch election whereby taxpayers may opt to align characterization of payments with the treatment in the payee jurisdiction under Law 2/2021 to avoid double non-taxation, with election consistency requirements under the EU Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido (IVA), the Spanish Value Added Tax harmonized with the EU VAT Directive (Directive 2006/112/EC); administered by AEAT.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: 0 EUR — every entrepreneur or professional carrying out taxable economic activity in Spanish territory must register for VAT; small traders may use the simplified regime (régimen simplificado) while turnover remains below 250,000 EUR; intra-community distance sellers of goods must register in Spain only when the annual dispatch volume exceeds 10,000 EUR, unless they voluntarily opt for OSS registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Spain mandates real-time VAT informational clearance through the SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) for taxpayers with annual turnover above 6,000,000 EUR: transaction-level invoice records must be transmitted to AEAT via certified API web services or XML file upload within 4 calendar days for issued invoices and intra-Community operations, and within 8 calendar days for received invoices. The Ley Crea y Crece obliges all businesses to issue and receive electronic invoices (Facturae format or equivalent interoperable e-invoice) in B2B relationships from 2025/2026; under the Verifactu project, digital invoices must incorporate a unique integrity hash/signature and be integrated with accounting records, while SII-affiliated taxpayers must also obtain the relevant digital stamp and reconciliation reference before underlying invoice data is declared to AEAT.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of whole and skimmed milk powder from Spanish customs territory to non-EU destinations qualify for the 0% VAT exemption with credit to input VAT where: (i) the goods physically leave the EU within 90 days of supply; (ii) the seller is a Spanish exporter holding a valid NIF and EORI; (iii) the buyer is established outside the EU; (iv) the contract, invoice and shipping documents evidence the transfer of title and risk to the buyer on Incoterms basis; (v) the DUA (Documento Único Administrativo) is completed and accepted by Spanish Customs; and (vi) the exporter retains the proof-of-export file. Intra-Community supplies of milk powder to taxable EU customers are separately exempt from VAT where the customer's valid VAT ID is held and the transport documents confirm intra-Union movement.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DUA) in the electronic SGA system, with the Export Accompanying Document (EAD), the export summary declaration, and confirmation of exit from the customs office of departure
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill (Carta de Porte / Conocimiento de Embarque / CMR consignment note) evidencing physical shipment outside the EU within the 90-day window
Commercial invoice and packing list describing CN codes 0402.10 and 0402.21, weights, Incoterms, and dairy commodity particulars
EORI validation record and exporter master-file (ficha de cliente) for the non-EU buyer
Bank SWIFT credit advice or Inward Remittance Certificate (Certificado de Abono Exterior / Certificado de Cobro en Divisas) evidencing receipt of the export proceeds in a Spanish bank account
Proof of delivery or arrival certificate (resguardo de entrega / certificado de llegada) from the overseas consignee, recommended for audit-safe substantiation in milk-powder export files
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The 0% rate is provisional until AEAT completes documentary verification; failure to produce consistent proof of export results in a regularisation requiring the exporter to self-assess 21% IVA on the gross invoice amount, together with late-payment interest (interés de demora) and the full reversal of deducted input VAT. Under Ley General Tributaria 58/2003, penalties range from 50% to 150% of the amount clawed back, increased to 100%–150% where false invoices or knowingly fraudulent export documentation are used; if the defrauded amount exceeds 120,000 EUR, criminal tax fraud under article 305 of the Código Penal applies, carrying imprisonment and fines. The four-year statute of limitations is suspended or restarted in cases of concealment, and AEAT prioritises post-export verification (verificación posterior) audits for dairy commodity traders, cross-checking customs exit records with SWIFT/FX data from Banco de España and applying additional exchange-control sanctions where repatriation does not occur within the statutory deadline.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain) together with the Ministry of Economic Affairs and Digital Transformation and the Directorate General for International Trade and Investments, with European Central Bank supervision under the Eurosystem.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain is a Eurozone member with full convertibility on both current and capital accounts for EUR-denominated transactions. There are no general exchange control restrictions on profit remittance, dividend distribution, or repatriation of liquidation proceeds, provided that all corporate, tax, and AML/CTF compliance obligations are satisfied. Capital movements and payments are liberalized under EU Treaty provisions and Spanish external transactions regulations, but statistical declarations to the Banco de España are required for certain cross-border flows. For trade with non-EU countries and in non-EUR currencies, banks apply normal commercial due diligence and sanctions screening, yet no special convertibility license is required.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory export proceeds surrender requirement exists under Spanish law. Exporters are not compelled to convert foreign currency receipts into euro within a prescribed statutory timeline. All proceeds may be retained in the original currency or freely converted. However, the exporter must comply with statistical reporting obligations to the Banco de España, generally through the T-1 external transactions declaration or the relevant balance-of-payments reporting form, when the transaction value or settlement exceeds threshold amounts or when a Bank of Spain statistical file is requested. The obligatory reporting timeline is tied to the monthly submission cycle following the month-end when the operation takes place.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium. EEA-licensed financial technology companies and electronic money institutions operating under the PSD2 passport may provide client money accounts for the Spanish treasury function, but availability is limited for commodity trading structures with non-EU counterparties. Fully offshore EMI providers without an EEA passport are legally restricted from offering domestic account representation and euro-denominated services to a Spanish SL in a manner comparable to a regulated EU credit institution. The dairy commodity trading business is classified as low-risk for AML purposes, which improves the feasibility of using a reputable EEA fintech EMI for treasury settlement, but high-value trade finance, LC issuance, and cross-currency hedging must be routed through a licensed Spanish credit institution or an EEA bank with a Spanish branch.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is legally permitted in Spain under AML/KYC regulations where digital identity verification via qualified electronic signatures, video identification, and biometric verification are used. Nonetheless, for directors who are non-EU residents, for capital-escrow arrangements, or for commodity trading structures involving non-EU suppliers, most tier-1 Spanish banks impose a physical or notarial presence requirement: at minimum a signed power-of-attorney authenticated before a notary and apostilled, plus an in-person meeting with the bank's compliance officer at the designated Spanish branch. A remote opening is viable only where the director already holds EU digital identity credentials, a valid tax ID, and a verified business history, and even then the bank may require a local in-country legal representative for ongoing treasury operations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ownership opacity or indirect holding structures through non-EU jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified certificates of incorporation and good standing, full corporate-chain organizational chart with percentage ownership, passport copies and proof of address for all natural-person beneficial owners holding more than 25%, Spanish tax identification numbers (NIF) for the SL and its shareholders, sworn compliance declarations, and notarized resolutions of the board approving the account relationship.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of funds ambiguity for inbound capital injection from a non-EU shareholder
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed equity subscription agreement, notarized capital increase deed, bank statements for the last 6-12 months of the funding entity, audited financial statements or tax returns proving the legitimate source of funds, a written source-of-wealth declaration, and, if applicable, evidence of foreign investment authorization or statistical declaration filing with the Banco de España.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk invoice pattern or mismatched commodity trade documentation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Contract of sale or sales confirmation for raw milk powder, transport documents (B/L, CMR, FIATA), commercial invoices, packing lists, quality certificates from an independent laboratory, insurance certificates, customs declarations, and an explanation of the full trade flow from origin to final buyer showing no ambiguity in the counterparty chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or embargo exposure through counterparties, shipping banks, or payment jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed counterparty sanctions and PEP screening reports, SWIFT or payment routing pre-analysis, ultimate-beneficial-owner screening results, goods classification proof under the EU Dual-Use list confirming dairy products are not restricted, and a legal opinion or compliance certificate confirming that the trade routes do not touch sanctioned territories or blacklisted entities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax status mismatch or failure to evidence economic substance in Spain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Spanish corporate tax certificate, VAT registration and monthly/quarterly tax filings, social security registration certificate, Spanish office lease agreement, payroll records for local staff, board meeting minutes held in Spain, bank account in Spain used as the core treasury account, and evidence of actual commodity sourcing and sales decisions made from the Spanish premises.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Use SWIFT MT103 wire transfers from the non-resident shareholder to the Spanish SL's escrow or operational EUR-denominated account. The payment must include a clear remittance reference stating 'Equity contribution / capital increase' and must reference the existing capital-increase deed and registered NIF of the company. For capital injections in euro from EU jurisdictions, SEPA Transfers Settlements using the SEPA Credit Transfer standard and Target2 clearing infrastructure are acceptable. For non-EU injections, the bank requires the underlying corporate resolution, the sworn capital increase deed before a Spanish notary, and proof of registration with the Spanish Commercial Registry. Where the foreign investment meets Spanish foreign-investment statistical reporting thresholds, the notary or bank will coordinate submission of the post-closing declaration to the Ministry or the Register, and the operation must be declared to the Bank of Spain for the external transactions statistics file within the statutory monthly reporting deadline.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails are SWIFT MT103 for international telegraphic transfers and commercial letters of credit issued in conformity with UCP600 for high-value raw milk powder shipments. Within the Eurozone or EEA, euro payments are processed through SEPA Credit Transfers via Target2. Trade settlements to non-EU suppliers and processing plants can be made through direct correspondent banks in USD or EUR, using SWIFT MT103 with the relevant invoice reference, or via documentary collection/letters of credit under URC522 or UCP600. The treasury policy should segregate settlement accounts: one dedicated to trade payables with LC confirmation banks, and one for spot FX settlement, in order to preserve clean audit trails and reconcile clearings against customs declarations.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX spot contracts for EUR/USD and EUR/other fully convertible currencies
Deliverable FX forwards for firm-priced future settlements up to typical trade tenors
Vanilla FX options (call and put) for downside protection and upside flexibility
Cross-currency swaps for structural matching of EUR revenue with USD or emerging-market currency costs
Non-deliverable forwards in currencies subject to convertibility or settlement controls, provided the Spanish credit institution accepts the instrument and EMIR clearing/reporting obligations are met

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Accounts deposit (Depósito de Cuentas Anuales): Balance Sheet, Profit & Loss Account, Statement of Changes in Equity, Notes, Depositor's Declaration and, if applicable, the audit report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial of the company's registered office; electronic filing via the Registro Mercantil Central EXPEDIENTE/DTA gateway
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholders' meeting (Junta General) must approve accounts within 6 months of fiscal year-end; deposit must occur within 1 month after approval; for a 31 December year-end: AGM by 30 June and deposit by 30 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-deposit penalty under Ley de Sociedades de Capital art. 283: EUR 1,200–EUR 60,000 scaled to balance-sheet volume; after one year of non-compliance the 'cierre registral' blocks all subsequent registry acts (share transfers, appointments, capital changes), the Spanish functional equivalent of administrative strike-off; creditors or shareholders may then petition for judicial dissolution

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax return — Modelo 200 (Impuesto sobre Sociedades)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: AEAT (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria); mandatory telematic filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 25th day of the 7th month following fiscal year-end; for a 31 December year-end: by 25 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing recargo of 5%–20% plus statutory interest on the outstanding amount; failure to file within 12 months triggers a fixed penalty of EUR 1,500 (LGT art. 198); incorrect or understated returns attract penalties from 50% to 150% of the shortfall (LGT arts. 191–193); AEAT may embargo bank accounts within the enforcement procedure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial-owner declaration — Declaración de Titular Real (DUE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual re-confirmation within 30 days of the shareholders' meeting that approves the annual accounts (by 30 July for a 31 December year-end); update within 30 days of any notarized share transfer or change in >25% ownership or control
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Serious anti-money-laundering infringement under Ley 10/2010: fines up to EUR 60,000; omission blocks registration of the related share transfer in the Registro Mercantil and exposes the administrador to personal civil and regulatory liability

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Legalization of statutory books (Legalización de Libros): Libro Diario, Libro de Inventarios y Cuentas Anuales, Register of Members, Minutes Book
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial (annual presentation of the company's book file for legalization)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months of fiscal year-end, hence by 30 April for a 31 December year-end; in practice coordinated with the annual accounts deposit by 30 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to legalize renders the annual accounts deposit defective and prevents the registry from accepting it; the company remains in cierre registral, unable to register capital increases, new directors or share transfers; registry surcharges accrue for late presentation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Economic Activity Tax settlement — IAE (Modelo 848 self-assessment; Modelo 840 for registration, variation or cessation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: AEAT (quota payable to the State and the relevant municipal treasury under the company's IAE registration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual quota settlement window 15 September – 20 November; registration and variation declarations within 2 months of the triggering fact; IAE applies only when net turnover exceeds EUR 1,000,000
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment recargo of 5%–20% plus statutory interest; AEAT enforcement by embargo of bank accounts and tax refunds; failure to register or update the economic activity carries penalties up to EUR 6,000 under LGT art. 192

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual informative return of third-party transactions — Modelo 347
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a 31 December year-end: by 28 February of the following calendar year; mandatory when transactions with any single counterparty exceed EUR 3,005.06 in the year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fixed penalty under LGT art. 198 for late or non-filing, plus EUR 30 per omitted or inaccurate record with a minimum penalty amount; recurring non-compliance is reclassified as a serious infringement with fines up to EUR 60,000; data are cross-checked against supplier and customer VAT filings, triggering automatic AEAT inquiries

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit (auditor de cuentas) under Ley de Sociedades de Capital art. 263 when the SL exceeds at least two of three thresholds at the balance-sheet date for two consecutive years: (i) total assets over EUR 4,000,000; (ii) annual net revenue over EUR 8,000,000; (iii) average headcount over 50. Audit is also compulsory if the SL heads or belongs to a group required to present consolidated annual accounts, or if it holds a >20% interest in another company and meets scaling tests.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish GAAP: Código de Comercio arts. 34–49 and the Plan General de Contabilidad (PGC 2007 as amended), with the simplified PGC-PYME available for eligible small and medium companies; consolidated financial statements (if applicable) are prepared under IFRS-EU per Regulation (EC) 1606/2002; annual accounts must be expressed in EUR and filed in Spanish

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SL must file the Declaración de Titular Real (DUE) with the Registro Mercantil Central: initial declaration within 10 days of incorporation; annual re-confirmation within 30 days following the shareholders' meeting that approves the annual accounts; and an updated declaration within 30 days of any notarized share transfer or any change in the register where the ultimate beneficial owner (>25% shareholding or control) changes. Share transfers in an SL require notarized public deed unless the bylaws validly authorize private document, must be recorded in the Register of Members within one month, and the resulting ownership change must be reflected in the annual DUE confirmation.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro de Registro de Socios) — records shareholdings, transfers, usufructs and liens; mandatory for every SL
Minutes Book (Libro de Actas) — records resolutions of the Junta General and of the administrador(s) or the board

Register of Contracts with the Sole Shareholder (Libro de Registro de Contratos) — required when the SL has a single shareholder and contains all contracts between the sole shareholder and the company

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $1,200 – $3,500 per year (Madrid/Barcelona corporate-services market, including registered office, mail handling, annual accounts coordination, DUE filing, book legalization and registry-filing support; excludes notarial and government fees)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $8,000 – $16,000 per statutory audit engagement (ROAC-certified audit firm, stand-alone SL with trading turnover in the EUR 8M–30M range)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% general corporate income tax rate. Newly incorporated entities generally qualify for a 15% rate during the first profitable tax period and the immediately following tax period, subject to statutory exclusions and anti-abuse rules.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Spain permits tax credits for qualifying research and development, technological innovation, certain audiovisual productions, employment-related measures, and investments specified by law. Small entities may qualify for reduced rates subject to applicable annual legislation. Qualifying dividends and capital gains from substantial shareholdings may benefit from the participation exemption, generally subject to a minimum 5% ownership and a one-year holding-period requirement; the exemption is generally limited to 95% of the qualifying income. Tax losses are generally subject to utilization limits based on prior-year turnover: 70% of the tax base for entities with turnover below EUR 20 million, 50% for turnover from EUR 20 million to below EUR 60 million, and 25% for turnover of EUR 60 million or more, subject to a EUR 1 million minimum offset. A 15% minimum effective tax rule applies to certain large entities and tax groups.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200, Corporate Income Tax and Non-Resident Income Tax return for permanent establishments, filed electronically through the Spanish Tax Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria, AEAT) electronic headquarters using an electronic certificate, Cl@ve where permitted, or an authorized representative.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The return is filed within the 25 calendar days following the six months after the end of the tax period. For a calendar-year taxpayer ending on 31 December, the ordinary filing period is 1 to 25 July of the following year. If the tax period does not end on the last day of a calendar month, the deadline is calculated by reference to the corresponding statutory period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, Spanish tax identification number (NIF), registered address, tax period, legal form, activity classification, filing type, and status as a member of a tax group.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident shareholder is not entered as the taxpayer unless the Spanish entity is a permanent establishment or other Spanish taxable presence. Report the Spanish SL using its own NIF and legal form.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting result before tax derived from the approved statutory accounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use Spanish statutory accounts. Do not substitute the foreign shareholder's consolidated or home-country accounting result.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Permanent and temporary positive or negative adjustments for non-deductible expenses, depreciation, provisions, impairment, related-party transactions, hybrid mismatches, exempt income, and other differences between accounting and tax treatment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Adjust only items attributable to the Spanish taxpayer. Foreign parent-company expenses require an arm's-length allocation and evidence of direct benefit and deductibility.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses generated in prior periods and utilized in the current period, subject to statutory percentage limits, ordering rules, anti-loss-trafficking rules, and the applicable EUR 1 million minimum offset.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses of a foreign shareholder or foreign group company cannot be entered as Spanish tax losses. Acquired-company losses may be restricted where ownership and business-activity continuity conditions are not satisfied.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable base after adjustments and permitted loss utilization, multiplied by the applicable corporate tax rate, including any reduced rate or tax-group treatment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the ordinary Spanish rate unless the entity demonstrably qualifies for a statutory reduced rate. A treaty does not reduce the Spanish resident company's corporate tax rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Qualifying tax credits, participation-exemption adjustments, double-tax relief, withholding tax credits, and other legally available deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign withholding tax credits require documentary evidence, proof of payment, income attribution, and compliance with Spanish credit limitations. Treaty relief at shareholder level does not automatically create a Spanish corporate tax credit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Advance corporate tax payments, Spanish withholding taxes, and other credited payments made during the tax period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile Spanish withholding certificates and payment records. Do not claim foreign parent-company tax payments unless a specific Spanish relief provision applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net corporate tax after credits, withholding, and advance payments, with payment or refund instructions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payment must be made through an accepted Spanish payment channel or authorized bank arrangement. A foreign bank account does not change the filing obligation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of controlled transactions, related parties, transaction categories, amounts, and valuation information where required by the return or related information forms.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report transactions with the foreign parent, affiliates, financing entities, service companies, and common-control entities. Reconcile the disclosures with the Local File, Master File, invoices, customs records, and accounting ledger.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Electronic signature, representative capacity, filing number, and payment or direct-debit details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign director or shareholder may act through a Spanish tax representative or authorized adviser. The company remains responsible for the accuracy and timely submission of the return.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing without tax payable may generally attract a fixed penalty of EUR 200, commonly reduced by 50% for voluntary filing without prior notice where statutory conditions are met. Late payment or late filing with tax payable generally produces an extemporaneous surcharge of 1% plus 1% for each complete month of delay during the first 12 months; after 12 months, the surcharge is generally 15% plus applicable late-payment interest. Fraudulent, incomplete, or materially inaccurate returns may trigger additional penalties of 50% to 150% of the improperly unpaid tax, depending on concealment and aggravating circumstances.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 202, corporate income tax payments on account, filed electronically through the AEAT electronic headquarters.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Quarterly payment windows; generally 1 to 20 April, October, and December, with the final day extended to the next business day where applicable.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Payments are normally due during the first 20 calendar days of April, October, and December. The payment-on-account amount is calculated under either the prior-year tax-liability method or the current-period profit method where mandatory or elected.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: NIF, legal name, tax period, accounting period, and filing category.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the Spanish SL's NIF. A foreign shareholder is not the filer unless it operates the Spanish taxable business directly.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-period corporate tax liability or current-period taxable profit, depending on the selected statutory method.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure the basis reflects Spanish taxable activity and not foreign group-wide profit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Applicable statutory percentage multiplied by the relevant calculation base, less permitted credits and prior payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Retain reconciliation schedules showing the relationship between Modelo 202, Modelo 200, accounting profit, and tax adjustments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Amount payable, payment reference, and authorized Spanish or SEPA payment account.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm that the payment account and authorization remain valid for the Spanish entity and its tax representative.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late payment is subject to the statutory extemporaneous surcharge regime and, after the applicable period, late-payment interest. Incorrect advance-payment calculations may generate underpayment interest and tax penalties. Repeated non-filing may increase audit risk and support a broader assessment of corporate tax compliance.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% Spanish withholding tax on dividends and other profit distributions paid by a Spanish resident company to a non-resident, subject to domestic exemptions and applicable tax treaties. Dividends paid to a qualifying EU or European Economic Area parent may be exempt under the Parent-Subsidiary regime, generally requiring at least 5% ownership, a minimum one-year holding period or commitment, qualifying legal forms, subject-to-tax requirements, and anti-abuse compliance.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, obtain a current tax residence certificate from the recipient's foreign tax authority, verify beneficial ownership and treaty entitlement, confirm the applicable treaty article and limitation, and retain ownership, substance, anti-abuse, and payment documentation. The Spanish payer generally applies the reduced treaty rate or exemption at source when legally supportable and files the corresponding Spanish withholding return, normally Modelo 216, together with the annual informative return Modelo 296. If excess withholding is paid, the non-resident generally seeks a refund from the AEAT using the prescribed non-resident tax refund procedure and supporting tax residence documentation. A certificate of residence alone does not cure beneficial-ownership, principal-purpose, conduit, or anti-abuse defects.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: The domestic Spanish withholding rate is generally 19% for interest and royalties paid to non-residents, subject to exemptions, treaty limitations, and EU directives. Qualifying interest and royalty payments between associated companies resident in different EU Member States may be exempt under the EU Interest and Royalties regime if ownership, holding-period, legal-form, subject-to-tax, and anti-abuse requirements are satisfied. Tax treaties commonly reduce the rate to 0%, 5%, 8%, 10%, or 15%, depending on the treaty and income category. Treaty rates must be confirmed under the specific Spain treaty, and beneficial ownership and anti-conduit requirements must be documented.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 250,000 per related party and transaction category is a principal threshold for the exemption from certain formal related-party information obligations, subject to exceptions. Spanish Local File and Master File obligations are governed primarily by the related-party rules, group status, transaction nature, and applicable statutory documentation exemptions rather than by one universal threshold. Entities and groups with prior-year net turnover below EUR 45 million may generally use simplified documentation, but significant, high-risk, cross-border, restructuring, financing, intangible-property, and tax-haven transactions may require fuller documentation. The EUR 45 million threshold and the EUR 250,000 threshold must not be treated as a blanket exemption from arm's-length pricing.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain has no separate offshore-style Economic Substance Regulations regime. Economic substance is enforced through the General Anti-Avoidance Rule, conflict-in-the-application-of-tax-law rules, simulation doctrine, beneficial-ownership principles, controlled foreign company rules, hybrid-mismatch rules, treaty anti-abuse provisions, principal-purpose analysis, and the requirement that related-party transactions reflect actual functions, assets, risks, decision-making, and commercial benefit. A Spanish SL trading milk powder should maintain real management, personnel or outsourced operational capacity, inventory and logistics evidence, supplier and customer contracts, pricing records, banking control, customs documentation, and decision-making records consistent with its claimed trading functions and risks.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax fraud and aggravated tax fraud
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentional concealment of sales, fictitious expenses, false invoices, undeclared related-party income, manipulation of customs or inventory records, or use of sham transactions causing Spanish tax damage exceeding the criminal threshold.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax fraud generally becomes criminal when the unpaid amount exceeds EUR 120,000 for the relevant tax offence. Ordinary tax fraud may result in imprisonment of 1 to 5 years and a fine from one to six times the amount defrauded, together with restitution and loss of public subsidies or tax benefits. Aggravated cases may result in imprisonment of 2 to 6 years and a fine from two to six times the amount defrauded.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto managers who knowingly participate may face criminal prosecution, imprisonment, fines, disqualification from public office or subsidized activities, civil restitution, subsidiary liability for tax debts, asset seizure, and precautionary measures. Travel restrictions may be imposed by a court where necessary to secure proceedings; there is no automatic travel ban for every tax assessment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: False invoicing, accounting manipulation, and concealed turnover
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Issuing or receiving invoices for non-existent transactions, double invoicing, off-book cash sales, falsifying warehouse receipts, or recording fabricated procurement costs in the milk-powder trading business.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative tax penalties may generally range from 50% to 150% of the unpaid or improperly claimed tax, depending on concealment, repeated conduct, fraudulent means, and cooperation. Conduct satisfying criminal thresholds may additionally trigger imprisonment and criminal fines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur personal civil and tax liability where the company is used to commit or facilitate the infringement, and criminal liability where intent and participation are established. Corporate limited liability does not protect a director from sanctions for personal misconduct.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Purchasing or selling milk powder at non-arm's-length prices, assigning margin to a low-substance foreign affiliate, undocumented shareholder loans, excessive management fees, or royalty and financing charges unsupported by functions and benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The AEAT may make a primary transfer-pricing adjustment, impose secondary tax consequences, deny deductions, reassess withholding tax, and impose documentation or valuation penalties. Failure to provide required documentation or providing materially incorrect documentation can generate fixed or percentage-based penalties under Spanish tax law, subject to statutory caps and safe-harbour rules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face subsidiary tax liability and sanctions where they deliberately approve non-arm's-length arrangements, conceal records, or obstruct an audit. Good-faith reliance on a properly prepared Local File does not eliminate the company's primary tax exposure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Misstating the origin, customs value, tariff classification, quantity, destination, or VAT treatment of imported or intra-EU milk powder; failing to document intra-Community supplies; or claiming input VAT without valid commercial evidence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Customs and VAT reassessments may include unpaid duty or VAT, late-payment interest, administrative penalties commonly calculated by reference to the tax or duty improperly avoided, seizure or forfeiture of goods, and suspension or loss of customs simplifications. Deliberate evasion may create criminal tax or customs exposure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and customs representatives may be jointly or subsidiarily liable where they knowingly submit false declarations or negligently fail to maintain required controls. Criminal proceedings may result in imprisonment, fines, confiscation, and civil restitution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company, sham residence, and treaty abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Spanish SL solely as a conduit, maintaining nominee directors without genuine control, routing dividends, interest, or royalties through Spain without functions or risk, or claiming treaty benefits while the foreign recipient is not the beneficial owner.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Spain may deny treaty relief, apply full domestic withholding, recharacterize transactions, assess interest and penalties, apply anti-abuse or simulation rules, and deny deductions. A shell company is not unlawful merely because it has limited operations, but sham activity, concealment, and abusive tax arrangements may create administrative or criminal liability.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil restitution, subsidiary tax liability, disqualification, asset-preservation orders, and criminal liability if they knowingly implement sham structures or false residence claims. Judicial travel restrictions may be ordered in criminal proceedings but are not automatic.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting unexplained third-party payments, structuring cash receipts, using anonymous or nominee ownership, failing to identify beneficial owners, ignoring sanctions or adverse-media indicators, or processing trade-finance payments inconsistent with the commercial transaction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Spain's AML framework, serious infringements may attract fines up to the greater of EUR 60,000 or the applicable statutory percentage of turnover, and very serious infringements may attract fines up to EUR 5 million or the applicable statutory percentage of turnover, together with public or professional sanctions and possible management disqualification. Exact amounts depend on the infringement, benefit obtained, recurrence, and responsible person.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers, and beneficial owners may be personally sanctioned where they participated in, consented to, or negligently permitted the breach. Criminal money-laundering liability may involve imprisonment, fines, confiscation, and civil restitution. Courts may impose precautionary travel restrictions in criminal cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to retain books, invoices, customs evidence, and tax documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Destroying or withholding accounting ledgers, bank records, contracts, warehouse records, transport documents, customs declarations, transfer-pricing files, or beneficial-ownership evidence during the statutory retention period or an audit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The AEAT may impose accounting and information-obstruction penalties, reject deductions, estimate the tax base indirectly, and apply audit-related sanctions. Obstruction, resistance, or refusal to supply information may generate escalating fixed and percentage-based penalties under the General Tax Law.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for deliberate destruction, obstruction, or falsification. The company may suffer adverse evidentiary presumptions, while directors may face civil restitution, tax subsidiary liability, disqualification, and criminal exposure where document destruction forms part of fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends without distributable profits, impairing statutory capital, making disguised distributions to shareholders, or using shareholder loans to bypass withholding tax and corporate-law restrictions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Improper distributions may be subject to repayment, dividend reclassification, withholding tax, corporate tax adjustments, director liability, and corporate-law sanctions. Shareholders who receive unlawful distributions may be required to restore them when statutory knowledge and repayment conditions are met.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be jointly liable for restoration of unlawfully distributed amounts, damages to the company and creditors, and subsidiary tax liabilities. Intentional concealment or asset stripping may also support insolvency, fraud, or criminal proceedings.
